followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Colombian regional-election restrictions on international river departure authorisations. They are intentional frontier movement measures represented as orders rather than observed complete stoppages. Retain Colombian- and foreign-flag vessel departures under the five named captaincies, with humanitarian/necessity authorisation. Neither incoming traffic in every direction nor ordinary land-border admission is added. Retain R1’s 24–27 October and R2’s 26–27 October 2019 ordered date windows, respectively three and one calendar-day differences. The shared 16:00 scheduled endpoint is not actual return, and no continuous enforcement is asserted. Retain Electoral politics / Election administration and security and Security / Public order and immediate safety. DIMAR expressly links the orders to the election; the official decree catalogue title supplies the public-order purpose with metadata-only access disclosed. DIMAR is the primary operational-order publication. The judiciary source is official decree metadata, not a full operative-text read or an independent enforcement source. Historical national-border stories do not expand these scoped phases. Retain separate unlocated captaincy/frontier text and null coordinates for both ordered phases. River departure scope is not converted into an all-land border line.
